guide.description: sort reorders its input lines. By default it sorts alphabetically; -n switches to numeric order (alphabetical would put '10' before '9'). It's most often used right before uniq, since uniq only collapses lines sitting next to each other.

flags.desc: drop duplicate lines, keeping only unique ones

examples.note: alphabetical works fine here since these are all 3-digit codes
-u sorts and dedupes in one step

exercises.title: Sort lines with sort
exercises.task: Take the status codes from access.log and sort them so identical values sit next to each other.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

exercises.title: Reverse the order
exercises.task: Sort the status codes again, but this time highest-first, using -r.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users

exercises.title: Sort and dedupe with -u
